facts.statement: Ludodactylus is a pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Aptian stage found in the Crato Formation of the Araripe Basin in Ceará, Brazil.
facts.quote: Ludodactylus (meaning "play finger") is a genus of anhanguerid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (Aptian stage) of what is now the Crato Formation of the Araripe Basin in Ceará, Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus Ludodactylus was named by Eberhard Frey and colleagues in 2003 and contains the single species L. sibbicki.
facts.quote: The genus was named by Eberhard Frey et al. in 2003 and contains one known species, Ludodactylus sibbicki.

facts.statement: The generic name Ludodactylus combines the Latin word for 'play' and the Greek word for 'finger'.
facts.quote: The name is derived from Latin ludus, "play" and Greek daktylos, "finger".

facts.statement: Ludodactylus was remarkable because it possessed both teeth and a Pteranodon-like head crest, a combination previously unknown in real animals but common in toy models.
facts.quote: The generic name Ludodactylus refers to the fact that the animal had the combination of teeth and a Pteranodon-like head crest, similar to many toy pterosaurs, and no such creature was known to exist until the discovery of Ludodactylus.

facts.statement: Unlike other ornithocheirids, Ludodactylus lacked a crest on its snout but possessed a crest at the back of its skull.
facts.quote: Unlike other ornithocheirids (the group of which Ludodactylus was originally assigned to), it had no premaxillary crest on the snout, but did have a crest at the back of the skull.

facts.statement: A yucca leaf trapped in the jaw suggests the animal caught it in its beak, failed to remove it, and likely died from starvation or related complications.
facts.quote: Trapped between the rami of the mandible is a yucca leaf; Frey suggested that the animal got it caught in its beak and unsuccessfully tried to dislodge it (the edge of the leaf is frayed), and then possibly died from starvation or a complication of starving.

facts.statement: The skull of Ludodactylus measured more than 66 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The skull would have been more than 66 centimeters (26 in) long.

facts.statement: The wingspan of Ludodactylus has been estimated at four meters.
facts.quote: La envergadura se ha estimado en cuatro metros.

facts.statement: A 2014 cladistic analysis by Brian Andres and colleagues placed Ludodactylus as a derived member of Anhangueria, closely related to both ornithocheirids and anhanguerids.
facts.quote: In 2014 however, Brian Andres and colleagues, in a large cladistic analysis of pterosaurs, found Ludodactylus to be slightly more closely related to ornithocheirids and anhanguerids than to Brasileodactylus.

facts.statement: An extensive 2013 cladistic analysis by Andres and Myers found Ludodactylus to be more closely related to ornithocheirids and anhanguerids than to Brasileodactylus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Andres y Myers (2013), en un extenso análisis cladístico de los pterosaurios, hallaron que Ludodactylus estaría algo más emparentado con los ornitoqueíridos y anhanguéridos que a Brasileodactylus.

facts.statement: Ludodactylus lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2007, Eberhard Frey suggested that Ludodactylus might be a junior synonym of Brasileodactylus, though later analyses disagreed with this view.
facts.quote: In 2007, Frey had reconsidered the validity of Ludodactylus, suggesting that it may represent the same animal as Brasileodactylus, and therefore a junior synonym.
